# dsh-branch-flow
**English** | 简体中文
A branch-flow panel for the DSH Web GUI. A status chip sits inside the composer; click it to open th
e full branch / commit / merge panel.
It removes the mechanical loop after editing code — staging, writing a commit message, switching bra
nches, pulling, merging, pushing — and validates branch names and commit messages against your team'
s conventions as you type.
## Screenshots
The branch chip in the composer. Click it to open the panel:
The full panel — commit changes, merge into a target branch, branch list, create branch:

### Version
The current version is in the `version` field of `package.json` and in Releases. To upgrade, replace
the tag above with the new version number.
### Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2` (`dsh.engines.dsh`)
- The host must provide the `webServer`, `subprocess`, and

`workspaceRegistry` services
- AI features (branch-name and commit-message generation) need the host
to compose `llm` and `agentDefaultModel`; when either is missing the panel reports an explicit erro
r instead of failing silently
## Interface
- **Status chip** (inside the composer, immediately left of the model selector): branch name + statu
s dot (green = clean, yellow = changes, red = conflicts) + change count + `↑`/`↓` ahead/behind. Clic

k it to open the panel. The row above the composer stays free.
- **Panel**: commit changes → push br
anch → merge into a target branch (headings carry no numbering), plus the branch list and branch cre

ation. Every action is button-driven; the plugin registers no model-facing tools.

t has two collapsible groups**:

## Security boundary
**It collects and uploads nothing.** The only remote access is `git fetch` / `git push` against the
`origin` you configured. There is no telemetry, no usage reporting, and no external HTTP request (th
e only `fetch` is the browser calling back to the local host at the relative path `branch-flow/*`).
**What it can do** (the permission surface a code audit should look at):
| Capability | Scope |
| Spawning processes | Runs `git` only, passing an `argv` array to `spawn` — **no shell**, so there

is no command injection |
| Reading files | Only `existsSync` to test whether an operation marker in

the git directory (`MERGE_HEAD` and friends) exists |
| Writing files | **None.** The plugin writes

no files; git writes the repository itself |
| Network | `git fetch`/`push` against `origin` only;

no third-party services |
| Runtime dependencies | **Zero npm dependencies**: the host half uses onl
y `node:fs`/`node:path`, the browser half only `require('react')` (host-provided) |
**Access fences** (all covered by regression tests):
- The host `/branch-flow/*` accepts only paths of **registered workspaces** (exact `realpath` compar

ison); the browser cannot make the host run git against arbitrary directories;
- Loopback access onl
y; requests carrying `X-Forwarded-For` / `CF-Connecting-IP` are refused outright; `content-type: app

lication/json` is required (which blocks cross-site forms);
- **A branch name cannot become a git op
tion**: ref names starting with `-` or containing control characters are refused (`invalid-ref-name`

), ruling out parameter injection such as `-D` or `--upload-pack=…`;
- Commit messages and branch na

mes are validated on **both the client and the host**, with the host authoritative;
- The plugin reg
isters no model-facing tools, so the model cannot commit or push on its own; AI is invoked only **wh
en you click a button**, and only branch-name/commit-message drafts or a requirement description are

sent;
- Refreshing relies on window focus plus visible-tab polling (panel 10s, chip 30s); a hidden
tab spawns no git processes, and no SSE connection is held open.
[该节后续省略]
## Caveats
Worth knowing before you use it:
1. **It runs with your privileges.** Installing a plugin means allowing that code to execute git com
mands on your machine. This plugin confines itself to running git against registered workspaces, wit
h regression tests covering that, but it is still a program holding your account's permissions — as
with any DSH plugin, trust the source before installing.
2. **`git push` really changes the remote.** Both "one-click" and "push" push to your configured `or
igin`, and "merge" pushes the target branch on success. **Verify in a test repository first**, confi
rming the branch name, merge direction, and push target behave as expected before using it on a real
repository. `production6` is protected as a baseline (it cannot be a merge target and cannot be del
eted), but pushes to targets such as `stage` are real.
3. **AI features send content to your model provider.** "AI polish" (commit message) sends a staged
diff fragment (up to 12 KB) to your configured default model; "AI suggest name" sends only the requi
rement description you typed, no code. If a diff contains secrets, tokens, or internal addresses, us
e "From the diff" (pure local assembly) or write the message by hand.
4. **The licence is MIT.** You may use, modify, and redistribute it freely, including commercially;
the author provides no warranty for the consequences of use. If you redistribute it, keep the copyri
ght notice in the `LICENSE` file.
